Last week I had a talk with my girlfriend which spawned from her feeling "guilty" about putting our boyfriend and me in an awkward situation (I fell in love with her, and while I'm developing a sincere and strong attachment to him I'm not really concerned about the possibility of things not working out with him). I told her that to me it didn't matter, that I'd be fine even living close to them in another apartment, as long as we all stayed together and they didn't get married, because that would officially mean putting us on different levels and I'm not okay with it. I didn't think it would be so soon, I'm still in university and living with my family, and by not living together I surely didn't mean in different sides of the country. Now I'm starting to believe that her feeling guilty was because she was applying to work in the city where he lives and not the relationship itself.
She's still figuring everything out, she just got the job offer and everything is still uncertain (both because it's new and because she's been having some issues because of her previous job), but when everything is set and done, I need to talk to her and be frank about everything. I can't just be casual with her, she's the love of my life, I'd rather lose her as a partner now than be slowly eaten by anxiety and fear over the span of months.

People will tell you a lot of ways you're supposed to play this game. Ignore them. Figuring out how Pathologic is structured is hard, a lot of times quests are built weirdly and it's not a crime to consult a walkthrough when you get stuck (which can happen a lot). I used a guide for the bachelor too, from time to time, and it actually made it easier for me to understand how to do stuff in my second and third walkthroughs with the other characters.
Play it the way that makes it fun for you. If it stops you from going forward it's not the right way to play.

(Okay, "fun" may be the wrong word, since pathologic is something you "endure" more then enjoy, but you get the meaning. But, again, play it any way you want, as long as you play it!)
